native.summary: A multipolar neuron: dendrites, a cell body with nucleus, nucleolus, Nissl substance (rough ER), Golgi and mitochondria, the axon hillock and initial segment, an axon wrapped in myelin with nodes of Ranvier, and axon terminals with boutons. Two enlargements: a node of Ranvier with its sodium channels, and an excitatory synapse with vesicles, active zone, calcium channels, AMPA receptors and the postsynaptic density.
native.scale_note: Three scales. The whole neuron is schematic (proportions chosen for clarity, axon shortened, sodium channels drawn far larger than life). The node of Ranvier enlargement is to true scale: 1 unit = 5 nm. The synapse enlargement is to true scale: 1 unit ≈ 5.9 nm (vesicles about 40 nm, cleft about 24 nm). No single ruler applies to the whole model.

Whole model.note: The whole neuron (top), with an enlarged node of Ranvier (bottom left) and an enlarged synapse (bottom right). Each enlargement has its own scale.

Neuron.note: Multipolar neuron: dendrites and cell body, the axon hillock and initial segment, the myelinated axon with its nodes of Ranvier, and the axon terminals.

Cell body and organelles.note: Through the window in the cell body: the nucleus with its nucleolus, rough ER (Nissl substance) with ribosomes, the Golgi apparatus and mitochondria. The axon hillock, on the right, has no Nissl substance.

Myelin and nodes of Ranvier.note: Myelin segments separated by bare nodes of Ranvier with their sodium channels (enlarged). One segment is cut open to show the axon inside.

Axon terminals.note: The axon loses its myelin and branches into terminals that end in synaptic boutons.

Node of Ranvier (detail).note: An enlarged node of Ranvier at true scale: bare axon membrane between the paranodal loops of the myelin on each side, with sodium channels and the spectrin scaffold underneath.

Sodium channels at the node.note: Three NaV1.6 sodium channels (α pore subunit with its β1 subunit) set in the nodal membrane, at true molecular size.

Synapse.note: An excitatory synapse at true scale: the axon swells into a bouton full of vesicles with a mitochondrion, facing a dendritic spine across the synaptic cleft.

Bouton contents.note: Inside the bouton: synaptic vesicles, a mitochondrion with cristae and microtubules arriving from the axon.

Release site and receptors.note: The active zone: docked vesicles, one fusing and releasing glutamate, calcium channels in the presynaptic membrane, and AMPA receptors on the spine above the postsynaptic density.

parts.name: Node of Ranvier 1
parts.description: Node of Ranvier 1: a short gap between two myelin segments where the axon membrane is bare. Voltage-gated sodium channels cluster here, so the action potential jumps from node to node (saltatory conduction). Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Exposed nodal axolemma · node 1

parts.name: Cell body (soma)
parts.description: The cell body (soma or perikaryon): it holds the nucleus and the protein-making machinery (rough ER as Nissl substance, Golgi) and integrates the inputs arriving from the dendrites. A window is cut in its front to show the inside. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Soma cell envelope

parts.name: Dendrites
parts.description: Dendrites: tapering, branching processes that receive synaptic input from other neurons and carry it toward the cell body. This multipolar neuron has several primary dendrites. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Compact dendritic tree

parts.name: Axon hillock
parts.description: Axon hillock: the cone where the axon leaves the cell body. It lacks Nissl substance (no rough ER), which is how it is recognised in stained sections. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Axon hillock

parts.name: Axon initial segment
parts.description: Axon initial segment: the unmyelinated first part of the axon, rich in sodium channels. The action potential usually starts here. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Unmyelinated initial segment

parts.name: Axon
parts.description: Axon: a single long process that carries action potentials away from the cell body. It runs through the myelin sheath and is bare only at the nodes of Ranvier. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Single continuous axon

parts.name: Axon terminals and boutons
parts.description: Axon terminals: the axon loses its myelin and branches (the terminal arbor), each branch ending in a swelling, the synaptic bouton, that releases neurotransmitter. One synapse is enlarged below. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Unmyelinated terminal arbor and boutons

parts.name: Cell body window: cut edge
parts.description: Cut edge of the teaching window in the cell membrane; the window itself is not a real opening.
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Soma cutaway material rim

parts.name: Nuclear envelope: outer membrane
parts.description: Outer membrane of the nuclear envelope, continuous with the rough ER. The large, pale, round nucleus with a prominent nucleolus is typical of a neuron. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.normal_ownership: Smooth convex shell and cut material rim use duplicated boundary positions for separate normals; welded geometric shell stays closed.
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Nuclear envelope · outer membrane

parts.name: Nuclear envelope: inner membrane
parts.description: Inner membrane of the nuclear envelope. The window cut into it shows the nucleolus. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.normal_ownership: Smooth convex shell and cut material rim use duplicated boundary positions for separate normals; welded geometric shell stays closed.
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Nuclear envelope · inner membrane

parts.name: Nucleolus
parts.description: Nucleolus: the prominent dark body inside the nucleus where ribosomes are assembled. It is large in neurons because they make so much protein. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Nucleolus · within nuclear interior

parts.name: Rough ER (Nissl substance)
parts.description: Stacks of rough endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes. In stained sections they appear as the basophilic Nissl bodies of the cell body and proximal dendrites; they are absent from the axon hillock. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Selected rough-ER/Nissl sheet neighborhoods

parts.name: Ribosomes on the rough ER
parts.description: Ribosomes bound to the rough ER, drawn enlarged so they can be seen. They make membrane and secreted proteins. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Rough-ER-bound ribosomes · enlarged symbols

parts.name: Golgi apparatus
parts.description: Golgi apparatus: a curved stack of flattened cisternae next to the nucleus that processes and sorts proteins from the rough ER. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Juxtanuclear Golgi · curved cisternal stack

parts.name: Golgi transport vesicles
parts.description: Small transport vesicles budding from the Golgi stack. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Golgi-associated trafficking profiles

parts.name: Cell body mitochondrion 1: outer membrane
parts.description: Outer membrane of a mitochondrion in the cell body. Neurons depend on mitochondria for the ATP that powers their ion pumps. It is cut open to show the cristae. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Somatic mitochondrion 1 · outer membrane

parts.name: Cell body mitochondrion 1: inner membrane and cristae
parts.description: Inner mitochondrial membrane folded into cristae, where ATP is made. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.source_name: Schematic neuron · Somatic mitochondrion 1 · inner membrane and continuous cristae

parts.name: Myelin sheath, internode 1
parts.description: Myelin sheath of internode 1: many layers of glial cell membrane (from an oligodendrocyte in the central nervous system) wrapped around the axon. It insulates the axon so the impulse can jump between nodes. At each end the layers turn in to meet the axon at the paranode. Overview proportions are schematic (lengths and thicknesses chosen for clarity).
parts.physical_role: wrapped glial lamellar packets with continuous paranodal ends
